title: Backward Engineering a Safety Case for AI-Generated Cryptographic Code

original_idea.body:
# Backward Engineering a Safety Case for AI-Generated Cryptographic Code

**Problem:** Define success: a complete formal safety case for AI-generated AES-256 implementation. Work backward to identify what formal specifications, proof obligations, and verification tools are minimally necessary.

**Direction:** Write a complete safety case argument structure for an AI-generated AES-256 implementation. Identify each assurance claim and the formal proof required to discharge it. Attempt to generate those proofs using Lean 4/Dafny. Measure which claims are provable today vs. which require future tool development.

**Why it matters:** Cryptographic implementations are the highest-stakes target for formally verified code. A complete safety case study reveals exactly which formal methods tools are missing and which are ready to deploy.

**Relevant context:** ATLAS pipeline generates verified Dafny programs including cryptographic examples. CSLib roadmap does not include cryptographic algorithms. RAND benchmarks include cryptographic implementations. This is a concrete backward engineering exercise.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Empirical analysis provides insights but safety impact is indirect
